newsitem.title: USA: Varlen sees steady transportation market pace.
newsitem.headline: Varlen sees steady transportation market pace.

text.p: Varlen Corp said Thursday it expects its underlying transportation market, which contributed to growth in first quarter earnings, will maintain its current pace this year.
The analytical instruments business will have a difficult second quarter comparison, it added, but is expected to build momentum throughout the year.

Varlen said its automotive products business should experience continued growth as General Motors Corp increases its light truck production and the first MD clutch program for Ford Motor Co begins to show results in the third quarter, Richard Wellek, president, said in a statement.

"We think the combination of acquisitions, new products, new markets, and increased market share should bring growth in 1997," Wellek said. "If the North American heavy-duty truck market maintains is current strength, this growth could accelerate."
Earlier, Varlen reported first quarter earnings of $0.63 per fully diluted share, vs $0.60 a year ago.
Sales in the quarter rose 34.8 percent to $124.0 million from $92.0 million.

"Varlen's record performance was achieved in the face of labor disruptions at General Motors and Chrysler (Corp ), two of our major automotive customers, and $850,000 in start-up and development costs of our Mechanical Diode (MD) one-way clutch for Ford," Wellek said.
He said the railroad products business had a slow start in the quarter, but picked up steam toward the end. He said original equipment manufacturer and aftermarket demand picked up strongly in April.
"Varlen's heavy-duty truck/trailer business benefited from higher than expected production industry-wide during the quarter," Wellek added.

The analytical instruments business, on the other hand, saw revenues decline 44.6 percent due to the sale of a non-core laboratory equipment business in July 1996 and lower sale and operating profit at the remaining quality control petroleum analyzer business.
